findings.text: The done-when's own gate is that tests/test_a_roadmap_read_answers_from_its_snapshot.py passes every case section 50 lists, and the file holds five cases where the section lists at least eight bullets: absent are (a) a fresh process answering its first call from the persisted snapshot within the same bound, (b) a write_plan made in one process forcing a second warm process to recompute with no window waited out, (c) a live run's exit record making the next call recompute and report it out of in_flight, with a patched _fresh_liveness turning false doing the same, and (d) advancing the clock past the stale threshold with every file unchanged reporting the run's new classification. The manifest concedes these under follow_ons (1) and (2), so the recorded gate does not assert the measure the done-when names.

The store-write case advances the generation through reckon._store.advance_write_generation directly rather than through write_plan, so the call in reckon/_store.py write_plan that advances the counter outside _write_plan_at_version (the change's central claim that every plan-state writer is covered) is never exercised: removing that call leaves all five tests green.

The counting_open wrapper rebinds builtins.open, but Path.read_text and Path.open resolve io.open, which rebinding builtins does not touch, so every Path-based read the key makes (.git/HEAD, the ref it names, the write counter and the snapshot file) is uncounted; the bound of at most 8 stat-or-open calls per mounted project therefore measures stats only and would not catch a key that added Path reads.

_roadmap_live_readings keys each live run on only the reduced [run_id, state] row, where section 50 specifies the key carry the watcher's _snapshot_reuse_key and its host-gated _fresh_liveness readings. A classification-input change that moves a run's detail while leaving state unchanged keeps the key matching, so the roadmap serves the older run rows until the revalidation window expires.
